[[File:Tom Braunlich 2022.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Tom Braunlich in 2022. Still: The Booster Pack Network.]]
'''Tom Braunlich''' co-designed Decipher's ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (SWCCG) with [[Rollie Tesh]]. His main contribution was the idea of using the draw deck as the player's Force.<ref name="bp-force">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=280s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 4:40–5:12. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref><ref name="wp-swccg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192945/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive].</ref>

== Before Decipher ==

Braunlich met Tesh through chess at Booker T. Washington High School in Tulsa, Oklahoma. ''Pente'' inventor Gary Gabrel recruited both as playtesters at Oklahoma State University, and both became ''Pente'' world champions.<ref name="rfd14-bio">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=62s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 1:02–3:08. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref><ref name="wp-braunlich" /> [[Warren Holland]] met them through Pente Games, which sold his ''Decipher'' prize puzzle.<ref name="rfd14-holland">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=248s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 4:08–4:39. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref> Braunlich holds a USCF Life Master chess rating.<ref name="wp-braunlich" />

Their early Decipher projects were the board game ''No Dice'' and the ''Star Trek'' VCR game ''Klingon Challenge''. Living on Bainbridge Island near Seattle, they met ''Magic: The Gathering'' designer Richard Garfield and pitched Holland a licensed card game. It became the ''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' CCG in 1994.<ref name="rfd14-trek">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=279s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 4:39–6:44. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref><ref name="bp27-magic">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zK_94pNOPTU&t=546s The Booster Pack #27 — The making of the Star Trek CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (10 August 2022), 9:06–10:30. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221006131804/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zK_94pNOPTU Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="st-timeline" />

== Designing SWCCG ==

Work on ''Star Wars'' began right after the ''Star Trek'' launch, before the license was signed.<ref name="bp-start" /> Braunlich and Tesh planned the game at designer Richard Borg's house in Florida. In 1995 they moved from Seattle to Virginia Beach to be near Decipher.<ref name="bp-start" /><ref name="pilot" />

The game started as each player building a base that the opponent tried to destroy. The base became the deck, and the deck became the Force a player spends and loses. Working out the Force pile and Used pile took weeks.<ref name="rfd14-force">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=616s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 10:16–12:19. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref> [[Destiny]] numbers replaced dice so the game needed nothing but cards. Strong cards got low destiny to keep decks balanced.<ref name="rfd14-destiny">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=767s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 12:47–13:19. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref><ref name="bp-destiny">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=600s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 10:00–11:03. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> Holland's interest in Joseph Campbell's hero's journey led to the split into Light Side and Dark Side.<ref name="bp-campbell">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=535s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 8:55–10:00. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref>

Braunlich worked 80 to 90 hours a week through 1995.<ref name="bp-hours">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=789s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 13:09–14:12. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> In the evenings Holland, Tesh, [[Jerry Darcy]] and others met in Braunlich's apartment. They projected proposed cards on a wall and reworked them one by one, often until 3 or 4 a.m. Holland approved no card he did not love. Braunlich proposed card functions and Darcy set the numbers.<ref name="bp-sessions">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=1283s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 21:23–23:57. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref>

Decipher bought a 70mm print of the films and an expensive editing machine to pull clear frames, even of background aliens. Skywalker Ranch let the team photograph props. Proposed lore went to Lucasfilm for approval, with sources.<ref name="bp-images">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=1047s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 17:27–19:43. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref><ref name="bp-lore">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=3403s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 56:43–57:43. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> A large spreadsheet assigned planned cards to future sets, and some [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]] cards carried icons that only mattered later.<ref name="bp-roadmap">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=2400s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 40:00–40:37. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref><ref name="bp-spreadsheet">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=3561s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 59:21–1:00:53. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref>

For the ''A New Hope'' launch in 1996, Decipher took the press out on Braunlich's boat, with David Prowse as a guest.<ref name="winter-press">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aq_dwh8Ojys&t=646s Inside the Star Wars CCG: Secrets from Decipher (Jason Winter interview)], Imperial Remnant (23 November 2025), 10:46–11:46. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015165322/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aq_dwh8Ojys Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Inside the Star Wars CCG: Secrets from Decipher (transcript)]].</ref> Braunlich attended the first World Championship, in Vail, Colorado ([[1996 Decipher World Championship]]).<ref name="bp-vail">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=1679s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 27:59–28:59. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> He answered players' emailed rules questions until he handed that job to [[Jason Winter]].<ref name="winter-rules" /> After the first year or two Braunlich stepped back from SWCCG as Decipher's design staff grew to about a dozen.<ref name="bp-later">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=2228s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 37:08–37:57. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> Former Decipher staffer [[Mark Tuttle]] called SWCCG "Tom and Rollie's … game."<ref name="fantha">[https://www.fanthatracks.com/interviews/guest-interview-mark-tuttle/ Guest Interview: Mark Tuttle], Fantha Tracks (15 March 2018). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195155/https://www.fanthatracks.com/interviews/guest-interview-mark-tuttle/ Internet Archive].</ref>

== Chess ==

In 1999 Braunlich said he "had a Masters rating in chess".<ref name="rfd14-chess">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=27s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 0:27–1:05. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref> He played in US Opens from 1976 and in the 2007 United States Championship, and his last FIDE rating was 2101.<ref name="chessgames">[https://www.chessgames.com/perl/chessplayer?pid=99037 Tom Braunlich], chessgames.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015182454/https://www.chessgames.com/perl/chessplayer?pid=99037 Internet Archive].</ref> Decipher's own introduction to SWCCG compared the game to chess; see [[Inspirations for Star Wars CCG#Chess]].

== Later Decipher work ==

Braunlich designed the battle system of [[Young Jedi]].<ref name="bp-yj" /> He was not involved in Decipher's later ''Wars'' game.<ref name="bp-wars">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=2805s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 46:45–47:17. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> He and Tesh began a ''Harry Potter'' card game for Decipher, in which players would cast spells by saying the words. Decipher did not get the license.<ref name="bp-potter">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=3061s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 51:01–53:07. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> He is thanked in the credits of the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] rulebook (2001).<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive].</ref>

The GeoCities anagram table unscrambles [[Nabrun Leids]] as Braunlich.<ref name="ana">[https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/anagrams.html Anagramed Decipherians]</ref>
